## Claims
- [computed] For \(J=[333,5^5]\subset\Lambda/I_{5,5}\), the accepted Smith witnesses give \(\operatorname{rank}Q_d=(1,1,2,2,2,1,1,0,\ldots,0)\) for \(d=9,\ldots,25\), and \(\operatorname{Tor}(Q_d)=0\) in every such degree. [artifact b5658ec18b84ad470751544a752f238dadd447fb7b1122a89a299a79e024042f]
- [proved] For \(P_{a,b}(z):=\sum_{\rho\subseteq b^a}z^{|\rho|}\), one has \(P_{a,b}=P_{a-1,b}+z^aP_{a,b-1}\), with \(P_{0,b}=P_{a,0}=1\). Hence \(P_{2,3}=1+z+2z^2+2z^3+2z^4+z^5+z^6=\binom52_z\).
- [source-backed] The lower-adjoined family indexed by \(\rho\subseteq b^a\) minimally generates the indicated basic ideal. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 220-235]

## Strategy
Use the symbolic rectangle-partition invariant, not further Pieri/SNF computation. Splitting \(\rho\subseteq b^a\) according as it has fewer than \(a\) positive parts or exactly \(a\), then subtracting \(1\) from each row in the latter case, proves
\[
P_{a,b}=P_{a-1,b}+z^aP_{a,b-1}.
\]
For \((a,b)=(2,3)\), this gives the computed rank polynomial:
\[
\operatorname{Hilb}_Q(z)=z^9P_{2,3}(z)=z^9\binom52_z.
\]
Thus the requested target is established for the specified computed case only.

## Gaps
The symbolic lemma counts the source-indexed generators; it does not prove that \(Q\) is torsion-free or has this Hilbert series for arbitrary \((a,b)\). The unresolved obstruction is precisely a uniform integral certificate identifying indecomposables with those generator degrees; no original failed certificate is established.
